item.title: Trapped in a Kill Zone, a Ukrainian City Is Beginning to Starve
item.description: Evacuation is almost impossible and food is running out in Russian-occupied Oleshky, a city menaced by mines and drones.
item.dc:creator: Siobhán O’Grady, Liubov Sholudko and Yurii Shyvala
item.media:description: A protester in Kyiv, the Ukrainian capital, last month calling for help for Oleshky, a city in southern Ukraine.

item.title: The Supreme Court’s New Term, and a Race for Nuclear Power on the Moon
item.description: Plus, why school music classes are under threat.
item.dc:creator: Will Jarvis, Margaret Kadifa, Jake Lucas, Ian Stewart, Ann E. Marimow and Selam Gebrekidan

item.title: A Supreme Court Battle Over Climate Change Begins
item.description: The justices are about to hear a lawsuit that could determine whether the oil industry faces billions of dollars in liability for damages caused by global warming.
item.dc:creator: Karen Zraick
item.media:credit: Mark Makela for The New York Times
item.media:description: Boulder has sued Exxon and Suncor saying they should help pay for the damage caused by global warming in the state. A Suncor refinery in Colorado last month.

item.title: How the Midterms Could Complicate the Supreme Court’s New Term
item.description: Even before the justices start their new term on Monday, the court has spent the summer resolving fast-moving requests on election-related disputes.
item.dc:creator: Ann E. Marimow and Abbie VanSickle
item.media:description: The court will hear oral arguments in about 60 cases starting on Monday and continuing through late April.

item.title: Congress Is Supposed to Be More Powerful Than the Supreme Court. Why Isn’t It?
item.description: Trump and his allies in the Capitol have revealed a problem that has been developing for decades.
item.dc:creator: Emily Bazelon

item.title: In a Major Boost for the Right, Another Bolsonaro Nears Brazil’s Presidency
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro’s first round lead leaves President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva three weeks to find the votes to stop Brazil’s, and Latin America’s, rightward shift.
item.dc:creator: Ana Ionova and Adam B. Ellick
item.media:description: Flávio Bolsonaro, the son for Brazil’s former president, Jair Bolsonaro, had the lead after Sunday’s vote.

item.title: Brazil Elections Head to Runoff Between Lula and Bolsonaro
item.description: Neither President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva nor Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of a former president, won the first round, but Mr. Bolsonaro took more votes.
item.dc:creator: Ana Ionova and Adam B. Ellick

item.title: Are Babies Conscious?
item.description: By pinpointing when it begins in young humans, scientists hope to better understand what consciousness is, and how it arises, in all of us.
item.dc:creator: Carl Zimmer

item.title: What Are the Biggest Questions in Science Today? 100 Scientists Weigh In.
item.description: We asked 100 scientists about unsolved problems in their fields. They sent back provocations — on the origins of life, the possibilities for human progress and much more.
item.dc:creator: Bill Wasik
item.media:credit: Photo illustration by Jane Stockdale for The New York Times

item.title: Spain’s Leader Calls Early Election After Housing Crisis Roils Government
item.description: Pedro Sánchez, the Spanish prime minister, has faced challenges including a migration crisis and several corruption scandals involving his inner circle.
item.dc:creator: Carlos Barragán and Jason Horowitz
item.media:description: Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez of Spain called an early election on Nov. 29.

item.title: Democrats Expect Record Number of Women in Party in House After Midterm Elections
item.description: Democrats are increasingly confident they will have a record number of women serving in the House next year, after backing women in competitive districts they are now positioned to win.
item.dc:creator: Annie Karni
item.media:description: “I’m incredibly confident that we will pass that 100 mark,” Representative Teresa Leger Fernández of New Mexico, third from right, chairwoman of the Democratic Women’s Caucus, said in an interview. “The real issue is how far above it do we go.”

item.title: Mayors Are Filming Videos, Mamdani-Style, With Varying Degrees of Cringe
item.description: The growing use of walk-and-talk social videos can be traced to Zohran Mamdani’s successful campaign for mayor of New York City. But not all candidates are naturals on camera.
item.dc:creator: Julie Bosman

item.title: Burst of Attacks in Gulf Heightens Fears Over Fragile Energy Trade
item.description: Strikes on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and oil infrastructure in Saudi Arabia came as the region’s exporters were getting more oil to the world market.
item.dc:creator: Lisa Friedman and Jenny Gross
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:description: Ships near the Strait of Hormuz last week. More tankers have moved through the strait in recent weeks.

item.title: Why Saudi Arabia’s Last War in Yemen Turned Into a Quagmire
item.description: A Saudi-led coalition has announced a military campaign against the Iran-backed Houthi militia in the country, reviving memories of its previous effort.
item.dc:creator: Ismaeel Naar
item.media:description: Smoke billowing from the fuel storage area at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, last month after the Houthis claimed to have attacked the facility.

item.title: Saudi and Yemeni Forces Attack Houthis to Retake Control of Red Sea Coast
item.description: The offensive is an effort to wrest control of the Bab al-Mandab Strait from the Houthis, a militia in Yemen backed by Iran.
item.dc:creator: Vivian Nereim and Saeed Al-Batati
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:description: Inspecting melted foam in a factory after a strike in Sanaa, Yemen, on Sunday. Houthi-affiliated media blamed Saudi Arabia for the attack.

item.title: Texas Pediatricians Face Paxton Investigations for Vaccinating Children
item.description: Ken Paxton, the Texas attorney general and Republican Senate candidate, has alleged a sprawling profit-driven conspiracy. Pediatricians say the accusations are an attempt at intimidation.
item.dc:creator: Christina Jewett
item.media:credit: Kaylee Greenlee for The New York Times
item.media:description: Dr. Rachel examining a patient in Texas last month.

item.title: Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine Is Awarded for Discoveries in Neuroscience
item.description: Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel were recognized for their work on light-gated ion channels and optogenetics, a technique that uses tiny lights to activate neurons in the brain.
item.dc:creator: Carolyn Y. Johnson and Leo Sands
item.media:description: Thomas Perlmann, the secretary general of the Nobel Committee, speaking at the Karolinska Institute in Stockholm on Monday.

item.title: Nobel Prizes 2026: What to Know
item.description: The recipients of the six awards in science, literature, economics and peace work are being announced this week.
item.dc:creator: The New York Times
item.media:description: A Nobel Prize medal awarded in 1998. Six Nobels are given each year.

item.title: Dennis Hastert, Powerful Politician Disgraced by Child Sexual Abuse, Dies
item.description: The longest-serving Republican speaker of the House admitted in 2016 to abusing teenage boys decades earlier. He was 84.
item.dc:creator: Carl Hulse
item.media:description: Dennis Hastert on Capitol Hill in 2003. He was sentenced to 15 months in federal prison in April 2016.

item.title: Karoline Leavitt, Trump’s ‘Machine Gun,’ Has a New Gig at Fox News
item.description: A fierce and nimble speaker, Ms. Leavitt is the second of Mr. Trump’s former press secretaries to join the cable news network.
item.dc:creator: Michael M. Grynbaum
item.media:description: Karoline Leavitt stepped down as President Trump’s press secretary and chief spokeswoman in August. She will start her new role with Fox News on Nov. 1.

item.title: 5 Challenges David Ellison Faces as Warner Bros. Discovery and Paramount Merge
item.description: The tech scion has given his combination of Warner Bros. Discovery and Paramount a new name: Skydance. Now he must make tough decisions about news, movies, streaming, sports and debt.
item.dc:creator: Michael M. Grynbaum

item.title: CNN C.E.O. Mark Thompson Says He Will Stay On Under New Owner Skydance
item.description: Mark Thompson told the network’s employees that he had faith that David Ellison, the chief executive of Skydance, would support “independent news that CNN has always stood for.”
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Mullin
item.media:credit: Dimitrios Kambouris/Getty Images for Warner Bros. Discovery
item.media:description: Mark Thompson, the chairman and chief executive of CNN, in New York in 2024. He told CNN’s employees on Monday that he would stay on after Skydance takes over.

item.title: Russia Moves to Tamp Down Rumors About Plague Outbreak in Siberia
item.description: The country’s consumer watchdog has said only that “an employee of an anti-plague institute in the Irkutsk Region” contracted pneumonia. Rumors and unconfirmed reports sounded a more ominous note.
item.dc:creator: Ivan Nechepurenko
item.media:description: An infectious-diseases hospital in the town of Shelekhov, Russia, on Monday. The mayor has urged residents “not to spread rumors.”
